target: Spoiler-free maximum verifiable completion of the 2011 Japanese mobile remake route

areas.name: Archival Remake Route
areas.location_cue: The preserved Japanese feature phone, carrier package, runtime metadata, and remake title screen.
areas.note: The chosen route is the 2011 remake; the earlier mobile version is not substituted for missing remake evidence.

save_backup.title: Duplicate the build before launch
save_backup.why: There is no verified replacement storefront or emulator route.
save_backup.detail: Copy every accessible application file and photograph the handset state before testing controls or network functions.

levels.1: The selected catalog route is a discontinued feature-phone remake.
levels.2: Use a lawfully preserved copy of the 2011 Japanese mobile release.
levels.3: Verify the Japanese title screen, 2011 build context, handset model, application files, and carrier metadata before play. A modern imitation or footage-only reconstruction cannot establish completion of this route.

levels.1: Several Japanese networks distributed the remake.
levels.2: Identify whether the surviving package belongs to docomo, au, or SoftBank.
levels.3: Photograph the handset and record the network branding, application identifier, file metadata, and launch path. Preserve each distinct carrier package separately rather than assuming their files are interchangeable.

levels.1: The required Flash generation depends on the carrier build.
levels.2: Record Flash Lite 3.0 for docomo or Flash Lite 2.0 for au and SoftBank.
levels.3: Confirm the runtime reported by the handset or preserved technical metadata before launching. Keep the phone firmware and browser version with the archive because timing and compatibility may change across implementations.

levels.1: The remake came through a monthly mobile service.
levels.2: Record the historical access price as 315 yen per month.
levels.3: Store any surviving subscription or carrier page beside the build. Treat 315 yen as historical context only; it does not identify a current lawful storefront or a working modern service.

levels.1: An older release exists outside the chosen route.
levels.2: Keep the 2001 version only as a historical comparison.
levels.3: Complete the 2011 remake for this pack. Do not merge screenshots, timing values, graphics, controls, or balance observations from the earlier mobile version into the remake checklist unless direct comparison proves they match.

levels.1: A working launch may be difficult to repeat.
levels.2: Record from application boot through menus, play, score result, and exit.
levels.3: Begin native-resolution capture before launch, include every input and result screen without cuts, and save the raw recording with the handset metadata. Duplicate both application data and footage to two checked storage locations.

areas.name: Operator Routes
areas.location_cue: The character-selection screen and the opening enemy formation.
areas.note: Player-facing text distinguishes the selections by mechanics and does not expose character identities.

save_backup.title: Preserve a neutral start
save_backup.why: Selecting an operator changes the active firing characteristics.
save_backup.detail: Keep a title-screen copy or reproducible relaunch state before recording either comparison run.

levels.1: One selection favors stronger individual shots.
levels.2: Choose the menu portrait whose weapon pushes targets back farther.
levels.3: Start a fresh run with the power-focused selection. Record the selection screen, then measure target displacement and time between shots against the same early formation used for the other operator; avoid assigning numerical stats without frame-tested evidence.

levels.1: The other selection trades impact for firing speed.
levels.2: Choose the menu portrait that can shoot more rapidly.
levels.3: Start a separate run with the rapid-fire selection. Capture identical early targets and compare shot spacing, knockback, reload timing, and survival margin with the power-focused run while keeping all unverified numerical values out of the guide.

levels.1: Both control styles need evidence from equivalent conditions.
levels.2: Record one comparable opening sequence with each operator style.
levels.3: Use the same handset, formation, capture rate, and input method for both runs. Compare only directly visible differences in impact and firing cadence, then retain the two recordings together so later hardware latency is not mistaken for character balance.

areas.name: Verified Defense Loop
areas.location_cue: The single-screen playfield, horizontal firing lane, approaching targets, and lower defense boundary.
areas.note: Only directly supported controls, reload behavior, and failure mechanics are stated as established facts.

save_backup.title: Capture controls before a full run
save_backup.why: A handset mismatch could make movement or firing impossible.
save_backup.detail: Record a short input test and verify native timing before committing the preserved build to extended play.

levels.1: The defense line is protected by lateral movement.
levels.2: Move sideways until the weapon is aligned with the approaching target.
levels.3: Track the target's lane, shift horizontally into alignment, and leave enough distance to recover from the next forced reload. Record the actual handset inputs because the surviving sources do not establish a universal key layout.

levels.1: Aligned shots are the only verified attack.
levels.2: Shoot the nearest target before it reaches the lower boundary.
levels.3: Fire while aligned, watch for visible recoil or backward movement, and prioritize the threat closest to the defense line. Keep shooting only as fast as the chosen operator and reload cycle allow.

levels.1: A hit creates space before it finishes a target.
levels.2: Use repeated shots to drive an approaching target away from the boundary.
levels.3: Confirm a hit by visible rearward movement, then use that space to address another lane or prepare for reload. The power-focused operator creates the larger displacement, but the exact distance remains unverified.

levels.1: Knockback alone does not clear the formation.
levels.2: Continue landing hits until the aligned target disappears or enters its defeat state.
levels.3: Maintain lane alignment through the target's full damage sequence and confirm the defeat animation before changing lanes. Do not infer a fixed hit count because durability can change later in the run.

levels.1: The weapon pauses after a short fixed firing cycle.
levels.2: Expect a reload immediately after every sixth shot.
levels.3: Count fired rounds from the last completed reload and create distance before round six. The reload begins automatically, so plan the final shot for the most urgent lane instead of spending it on a distant target.

levels.1: No shot can be fired during the reload pause.
levels.2: Use knockback and lateral spacing before the weapon becomes unavailable.
levels.3: Push the nearest threat back before the sixth round, begin the reload with no target touching the lower boundary, and reposition while firing is locked. Resume shooting only when the game visibly returns control.

levels.1: The run ends when an approaching threat crosses the protected boundary.
levels.2: Keep every target above the defense line at the bottom of the playfield.
levels.3: Watch the lowest target rather than the largest group. If a controlled archival attempt is available, capture one natural breach, the full result screen, and every retry or exit option without risking the only preserved session.

levels.1: Removing an ordinary formation advances the run.
levels.2: Defeat every standard target currently present on the playfield.
levels.3: Sweep lanes until no ordinary target remains, preserve the transition that follows, and continue recording into the next distinct encounter. Do not use a presumed stage number or order in the player-facing guide.

areas.name: Documented Special Encounters
areas.location_cue: The same defense playfield after an ordinary formation has been cleared.
areas.note: Physical descriptions replace identity names, and no encounter order is exposed.

save_backup.title: Keep the first complete encounter capture
save_backup.why: Later runs become faster and may not reproduce a clean recording.
save_backup.detail: Save each uninterrupted encounter recording and its preceding transition before continuing the survival loop.

levels.1: A tall single target replaces the ordinary formation.
levels.2: Continue clearing formations until the large upright target appears.
levels.3: Stay aligned with its lane, use early shots to preserve distance, and enter each forced reload with room above the boundary. Capture its full appearance, movement, hit response, defeat state, score change, and the next screen without naming its franchise identity.

levels.1: A long-bodied target creates a different defense pattern.
levels.2: Continue the run until the giant serpentine target appears.
levels.3: Record its occupied lanes and movement before committing to a firing rhythm. Use the chosen operator's knockback to protect the nearest boundary point, count every reload cycle, and preserve the complete defeat transition without exposing its identity.

levels.1: Several airborne targets share one special encounter.
levels.2: Continue clearing formations until the multi-target flock appears.
levels.3: Track each airborne threat separately, shoot the lowest one first, and avoid beginning a reload while another remains close to the boundary. Capture the full target count, movement, individual defeats, score changes, and completion transition.

areas.name: Escalating Survival Run
areas.location_cue: Later repeats of the defense playfield, transition screens, live score, and final result.
areas.note: The pack follows only the visible survival mechanics and does not describe story structure.

save_backup.title: Preserve the best complete attempt
save_backup.why: Later cycles increase pressure and a replacement session may be unavailable.
save_backup.detail: Keep the uninterrupted raw capture and score ledger before experimenting with additional runs.

levels.1: Clearing the documented encounters does not finish the survival run.
levels.2: Continue playing when the game returns to another defense formation.
levels.3: Treat the new formation as a later cycle of the same run, keep the score and operator unchanged, and continue until the result screen appears. Preserve the transition without assigning a stage number or narrative meaning.

levels.1: Later threats close the distance more quickly.
levels.2: Compare target travel time after each completed encounter cycle.
levels.3: Measure from a consistent spawn point to the defense line and record the cycle context. Adjust lane priority and reload spacing to the observed increase, but do not publish a multiplier until repeated footage confirms it.

levels.1: Later targets require more sustained fire.
levels.2: Count confirmed hits on matching targets across later cycles.
levels.3: Use the same operator and target type, exclude missed shots, and record the defeat frame. Plan extra reloads when durability rises, while leaving exact health and scaling values marked unverified.

levels.1: The survival attempt produces a score for comparison.
levels.2: Capture the score before play, after each transition, and at failure.
levels.3: Keep a ledger containing operator style, cycle context, formation result, special encounter, reload count, breach moment, and final score. Repeat comparable actions before assigning points or bonuses to any event.

levels.1: Maximum verifiable completion ends with a documented survival attempt.
levels.2: Continue the escalating loop until a target reaches the defense line.
levels.3: Record the entire longest lawful attempt, including the final breach and result screen. Archive completion requires every verified mechanic and encounter plus one uninterrupted attempt from character selection through that final result.

areas.name: Historical Network Ranking
areas.location_cue: The score result, upload prompt, carrier connection screen, and ranking table or error response.
areas.note: Rotating or discontinued network data is never presented as an ordinary requirement available today.

save_backup.title: Capture local results first
save_backup.why: Testing a retired endpoint may interrupt or alter the preserved session.
save_backup.detail: Save the local score screen and duplicate the build before attempting any network connection.

levels.1: The original release could compare scores through a carrier service.
levels.2: Open the ranking or score-upload option if the preserved build still exposes it.
levels.3: Capture the menu path, submitted score, connection request, endpoint response, displayed table, and date. If the carrier service no longer responds, retain the failure evidence and mark live placement unobtainable.

levels.1: A dead endpoint is an archival result, not a missing score target.
levels.2: Record the complete network error or unavailable screen.
levels.3: Preserve the unedited connection attempt with handset clock, network state, application version, and error text. Do not emulate a successful submission or invent a ranking threshold when the historical service cannot answer.

areas.name: Unverified Completion Boundaries
areas.location_cue: Any undocumented control, menu, statistic, wave, score, reward, save, or retry screen exposed by a lawful remake build.
areas.note: Unknown data remains visibly withheld instead of being padded into false completion instructions.

save_backup.title: Retain evidence before resolving a hold
save_backup.why: A single observation may reflect handset timing or an incomplete build.
save_backup.detail: Store the untouched footage and transcription, then require a repeat result before editing the fact notes or guide text.

areas.name: Final Archival Audit
areas.location_cue: The preserved remake package, operator captures, encounter index, score ledger, network evidence, and verification-hold list.
areas.note: This audit defines maximum verifiable completion for a discontinued mobile survival game.

save_backup.title: Duplicate the final evidence set
save_backup.why: The audit depends on irreplaceable original-device captures and branching operator runs.
save_backup.detail: Keep two checked copies of the build, raw footage, metadata, translations, and ledger before reconciling the final checklist.

levels.1: The completed archive must identify the exact release being played.
levels.2: Confirm the remake title screen, carrier package, runtime, handset, and two backups.
levels.3: Compare the device photographs, application metadata, carrier record, native capture, and backup checksums. Reject evidence taken only from the earlier mobile version or an unidentified reproduction.

levels.1: Both mechanical selections need comparable evidence.
levels.2: Confirm one captured run for the power-focused style and one for the rapid-fire style.
levels.3: Review the two opening runs under matching conditions and verify visible differences in shot impact and cadence. Keep exact statistics withheld unless repeated frame analysis establishes them.

levels.1: Every verified control and failure rule should appear in one continuous record.
levels.2: Confirm movement, firing, knockback, defeat, reload, formation clear, and a defense-line breach.
levels.3: Use the session index to locate each mechanic in uninterrupted footage. Check that the six-shot reload and firing lock are visible and that the breach result includes the complete retry or exit screen.

levels.1: Each documented physical encounter archetype needs a complete capture.
levels.2: Confirm the large humanoid, serpentine, and airborne-flock encounters.
levels.3: Verify that every recording includes the preceding formation transition, full encounter, defeat state, score change, and following screen. Keep franchise identities out of player-facing text.

levels.1: The archive must show how the survival run changes over time.
levels.2: Confirm a repeated cycle, faster movement, increased durability, final score, and natural failure.
levels.3: Compare timestamped examples made with the same operator and target type, then preserve the longest complete run and its score ledger. Leave unsupported scaling numbers and scoring formulas uncertain.

levels.1: A complete archival record separates known mechanics from lost data.
levels.2: Review every verification hold and attach direct evidence to any resolved entry.
levels.3: Keep unsupported holds marked uncertain. Replace a hold only after repeatable remake-build evidence establishes the exact value or behavior, and list all remaining holds in the report.
